author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Brielle Saracini marked the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks by throwing a ceremonial first pitch at Yankee Stadium, accompanied by retired captain Derek Jeter. The appearance renewed a bond that began after Saracini lost her father, Victor, the pilot of hijacked United Airlines Flight 175, when the plane struck the World Trade Center’s South Tower.

Saracini was a young Yankees fan when she first met Jeter, and their connection continued through milestones in her life. She later met her husband, Sean McGuire, at a camp for children who had lost a parent in the attacks. Their shared experience became part of a family story shaped by grief, remembrance and long-term support.

The first pitch placed a personal history inside a public commemoration, linking a New York sports institution with one family’s path over a quarter-century. Jeter’s presence reflected the value of relationships that continued long after the immediate aftermath. For Saracini, the moment honored her father while also showing the life built since his death. The ceremony offered a quieter measure of September 11’s legacy: connections sustained across generations, not only anniversaries.
dek: Brielle Saracini’s ceremonial first pitch renewed a bond formed after her father, Flight 175 pilot Victor Saracini, died in the attacks.
headline: Yankees fan honors father alongside Derek Jeter 25 years after September 11
